market_brief: With US cash markets shut for Thanksgiving (Wednesday: S&P 500 -0.25%, Nasdaq 100 -0.64%, VIX 28.3), Europe caught up with Wall Street's late reversal: Euro Stoxx 50 +1.9%, DAX +1.8% and STOXX 600 +1.5%, helped by banks, chipmakers and Reuters reports that EU duties under the proposed Section 301 tariffs would be capped at 15%. ECB accounts showed broad support for tightening and a December 17 hike to 2.75% is fully priced, while a far weaker-than-expected PBoC yuan fix (6.7096) signalled Beijing may let the currency absorb tariff pressure. Indian stocks closed modestly higher (Sensex +0.46% to 84,329, Nifty +0.25%) on a 3.7% IT rally after paring early gains, ahead of an expected RBI hike on December 4. Oil eased from Asia's $95 Brent spike (the dashboard's Brent contract shows $90.9, -3.9%; WTI $84.2) ahead of OPEC+ from Nov 29, while metals rebounded: gold +1.6% to about $3,593, silver +3.9%, copper +2.5% and natural gas +10.9%; the US 10Y sits at 4.85%, DXY 103.8 and bitcoin near $60,600.
ai_brief: Agent infrastructure led the day: Anthropic said MCP has passed 700m monthly SDK downloads with Tasks and Elicitation going GA, Cloudflare opened agent-facing site search, and OpenAI began enterprise trials of confidential 'Private Inference'. Open and efficient models kept coming, from PrismML's 5.9GB ternary coding model to Sand.ai's MAGI-2 video model. Policy pressure rose as New York banned AI chatbot toys and 42 attorneys general moved to block Character.AI's chat-data auction, while ElevenLabs ($33bn) and a16z (~$20bn) fundraising reports show capital still flowing.

items.headline: Europe rebounds about 1.5% as banks and chipmakers bounce; EU tariff fears ease
items.summary: The STOXX 600 rose about 1.4% early, reversing Wednesday's drop, with Deutsche Bank +3%, Soitec and Infineon about +4%, and Babcock +5.8% on an £8bn UK submarine-facilities contract. Reuters reported duties on the EU are likely to be capped at last year's agreed 15% rate under the proposed Section 301 measures.

items.headline: Update: Sensex closes +390 at 84,329 after paring gains; Nifty ends 25,885
items.summary: Change from the morning: indices finished well off intraday highs (Nifty touched 25,975) as consumer and financial names faded, leaving the Nifty +0.25% and the Sensex +0.46%. Nifty IT gained 3.7% while FMCG slipped 0.9%; mid and small caps rose 0.3-0.7%.

items.headline: HCLTech +6.4%, TCS +4.9% lead; Asian Paints and Bajaj Finance drop about 3%
items.summary: IT heavyweights and BSE (+5.7%) topped Nifty gainers, while Asian Paints, Bajaj Finance, Shriram Finance and Nestle India fell 2.8-3%. Prestige Estates (+8.7%) and MCX (+7.6%) led midcaps; FIIs and DIIs were both net buyers in the prior session.

items.headline: ECB accounts: many members could have backed an October hike; December move fully priced
items.summary: Accounts of the Oct 28-29 meeting show broad support for tightening, with the ECB holding only to gather more inflation data. Markets fully price a 25bp hike to 2.75% on December 17, per Reuters; Lagarde's term ends in February 2027.

items.headline: German GfK consumer climate edges up to -30.2, short of forecasts
items.summary: The December reading improved 0.7 points from a revised -30.9 but missed the -29.9 consensus; economic expectations fell 3.7 points as inflation worries returned.

items.headline: Update: Brent briefly tops $95 in Asia, then eases as markets look to OPEC+
items.summary: What changed: Brent hit about $95.3 early in Asia after the Ras Tanura strike claims, but the front contracts eased through the European morning (Feb Brent near $90 by midday India time) while WTI held around $84. The IEA flagged a 1.7m bpd October inventory build; OPEC+ ministers meet from Nov 29 on 2027 output.

items.headline: Gold and silver rebound 1-4% from lows; MCX silver jumps over 3%
items.summary: COMEX gold rose about 1.1% to near $3,575 and silver 3.5% to about $41.5 on bargain buying after this week's slide; MCX gold traded near Rs 1.22 lakh per 10g. An independent analyst cited $3,540-3,560 support and $3,640 resistance for gold.

items.headline: PBoC sets yuan fix at 6.7096, far weaker than the 6.6655 estimate
items.summary: The reference rate came in roughly 0.7% weaker than the Reuters estimate, a rare signal of tolerance for yuan softness as US tariff threats build; the PBoC also injected 571.5bn yuan via reverse repos.

items.headline: Hang Seng +1.2% as AI model makers Zhipu and MiniMax jump 7-8%
items.summary: The Hang Seng and Hang Seng Tech each rose about 1.2%, led by large-model stocks Zhipu and MiniMax, while gold miners such as Zijin Gold International gained over 5%; mainland shares were flat.

items.headline: Halfords soars about 14% after H1 profit jumps 66% and guidance is raised
items.summary: H1 revenue rose 6.7% to £953m and underlying pre-tax profit reached £39m, helped by about £8m from a warm summer; FY27 profit guidance was lifted to £60-65m.

items.headline: Microsoft carries a Sell call from Bears of Wall Street on AI capex and FCF squeeze
items.summary: The independent analyst, who cut the stock from Hold on Nov 17, points to a 27% drop in fiscal Q1 free cash flow to $18.6bn and forecasts gross margin near 63% versus a ~67% consensus, citing AI infrastructure costs and competition.

items.headline: Positioning: Goldman says hedge funds added shorts; ETF shorts post third-largest weekly jump in a decade
items.summary: investingLive's earnings-reaction gauge sits at 4.5/10, with the share of stocks rising on results down to 38%, even as S&P and Nasdaq futures have bounced about 5% from Nov 20 lows; it notes Goldman data showing five weeks of de-grossing followed by fresh shorting.

items.headline: Asia closes firmer: Nikkei +0.9%, Kospi +0.3% after Tuesday's 6.2% rout, ASX +0.8%
items.summary: Gains narrowed from the morning in thin holiday trade, per AP; Kospi's bounce was modest after its sharp fall earlier in the week, and USD/JPY held near 159.1.

items.headline: Calendar: US half-day Friday; OPEC+ from Nov 29; RBI Dec 4; FOMC Dec 8-9; ECB Dec 17
items.summary: US equities reopen Friday for a shortened session after Thanksgiving. OPEC+ meets on 2027 output from Nov 29, the RBI decides on Dec 4 amid hike expectations, the Fed on Dec 9 and the ECB on Dec 17, with hikes priced at both.

items.headline: MCP passes 700m monthly SDK downloads; Tasks and Elicitation go GA, Skills over MCP in beta
items.summary: Anthropic says the Model Context Protocol now has over 10,000 connectors; the update makes long-running Tasks and user Elicitation generally available and opens a public beta for delivering Skills over MCP.

items.headline: OpenAI begins limited trials of "Private Inference" for enterprise data
items.summary: Sam Altman said a small group of enterprise customers is testing confidential-compute inference designed so OpenAI cannot see their data; pricing, model coverage and GA timing were not disclosed.

items.headline: PrismML squeezes a 27B coding model into 5.9GB with all-ternary weights
items.summary: Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, built on Qwen3.8 27B and released under Apache 2.0, reportedly scores 75.6 on SWE-bench Verified versus 80.6 for the full-precision model.

items.headline: Sand.ai's MAGI-2 tops a video leaderboard at a fraction of ByteDance pricing
items.summary: The ~480B-parameter MoE video model generates up to 30s of 1080p video with audio, ranks first on Artificial Analysis image-to-video, and costs about $0.07 per second via API; flagship weights are promised without a date.

items.headline: Google Research posts six agent-generated math papers, including a factoring claim
items.summary: Papers produced by a multi-agent Gemini harness appeared in the google-research repo; the lead paper claims a new integer-factoring algorithm, but it is not peer reviewed and the promised Lean proofs are not yet posted.

items.headline: New York bans AI chatbot toys for five years
items.summary: Governor Hochul signed a ban on making or selling toys with embedded AI chatbots, effective in 90 days with penalties up to $15,000 a day; New York follows California.

items.headline: 41 states plus DC move to block Character.AI's auction of user chat histories
items.summary: The bipartisan AG coalition asked the bankruptcy court to stop a Dec 1 sale of private chats covering over 21m US users, including more than 2m minors' accounts.

items.headline: Update: Amodei rejects Axios report on AI and human free will as "absurd"
items.summary: Following Axios's story on internal model-release concerns, Anthropic's CEO denied the characterisation and said fully autonomous development of successive frontier models would not be safe.

items.headline: Anthropic study of 58 enterprise customers: workflow redesign beats tool training
items.summary: Interviews covering nearly 300 deployments found most value came from higher output and the best results from reorganising work; about two-thirds of firms said they hired less because of AI. The sample is Anthropic's own customers.

items.headline: ElevenLabs reportedly in talks at $33bn; a16z reportedly seeking ~$20bn of new funds
items.summary: ElevenLabs is said to be in early talks to raise at a $33bn valuation with ~$700m annualised revenue, while Axios reports Andreessen Horowitz is raising about $20bn less than a year after a $15bn close; neither is confirmed.

items.headline: Cloudflare launches "Search for Agents" beta on all plans
items.summary: A single toggle builds a site search index and advertises it to AI agents at a well-known endpoint; AI Search billing starts December 1.

items.headline: Trending: n8n's "nod" web agent and "timon" multi-agent coding daemon
items.summary: n8n-io/nod, an Apache-2.0 personal agent that asks before acting on websites, added about 1,000 stars this week; ai-timon/timon runs coding agents in separate git worktrees with a second model reviewing before merge.
